item.text: The Corruption and Crime Commission investigated possible public-officer misconduct in a murder investigation and the resulting prosecution and appeals.
item.support: whether any public officer engaged in misconduct in connection with the investigation

item.text: It examined police interviews, changes to witness statements, forensic testing and the disclosure of relevant material to prosecutors and the defence.
item.support: the duty of disclosure and the responsibility of police and other officers to make such disclosure

item.text: The Commission formed misconduct opinions about two police officers and a prosecutor concerning altered statements, misleading information and failures to disclose relevant material.
item.support: The Commission has formed a number of opinions as to misconduct and made a number of recommendations

item.text: The Commission made six recommendations addressing possible disciplinary action, interviews with mentally ill suspects, police training, written prosecution advice and a possible professional-conduct complaint.
item.support: That consideration is given by the Commissioner of Police to making special provision for the interviewing by investigating police of mentally ill suspects.
